direction.title: Margin front: feature at reading width
direction.summary: The lead story runs at reading width with an italic deck; secondary items run in a narrow margin column. Use for small editorial homes.

layout.skeleton: feature title across 8 cols, standfirst at 62ch; a 3-col margin column holds the secondary dispatch and a recipe card
layout.focus: feature title, with byline and read time from the brief
layout.desktop: asymmetric 8/1/3 split; the title breaks into the margin
layout.mobile: feature first, then dispatch, then recipe

imagery.subject: the feature's setting or material, top-down
imagery.fallback: an ink rule plus a large italic drop numeral of the read time

motion.trigger: Open the feature by tap or keyboard
motion.effect: Reveal the standfirst and underline the active link as the reading view opens
motion.reduced: Open the reading view immediately and preserve focus

action.instruction: Headline and button both open the feature
action.label: Read [feature title]

direction.why: Tactile, observant reading wants a comfortable measure and print logic: rules, margins and an italic voice instead of card grids.

sources.observation: Butterick: 'Aim for an average line length of 45–90 characters, including spaces.'

interaction.focus: Use a two-tone focus ring (2 px paper with 2 px ink outside) on the primary control.
interaction.accent_role: Use the accent as a focal fill under accent_foreground. Check contrast before using it as text.
interaction.keyboard: Expose the primary control by keyboard and announce pending and completed states.

assumptions: Use only the project facts and assets in the brief.
handoff: Apply the composition to the actual content. Preserve the task and brand constraints. Fill label slots only with facts supplied by the brief. Use the source as design evidence. Verify the action, reading order and legibility at 390 px.
